phase: The AM lane is back — and the money question finally has a number: $168 spent, 15 leads, zero confirmed booked calls (day 235 AM)
headline: Good morning — the AM brief is writing again. This run reached the Mac for the first time since Aug 28, so five dark mornings (Aug 29, 30, 31, Sep 1) end here. And it lands on a sharper fact than "the ads are running." The watchdog's own 5:36 PM scorecard says it out loud: cost per booked call is the deciding metric — and it is not evaluable, because no CRM source is connected and the Meta→CRM sync has been failing since Aug 27. So this is where the company actually stands this morning: $167.65 of the $300 plan spent (56%), 15 instant-form leads at an $11.18 CPL, every kill gate green, all six ads live — and zero confirmed booked calls. Not zero bookings; zero *knowledge*. Half the budget is gone and nobody can say whether it bought anything. Two of the last three leads made that worse, not better: Ben Garcia (TX) came in last night with an email and the literal field "Call — no number," on a form whose entire promise is speed-to-lead. Meanwhile the other funnel's digest reported "0 new leads in 24h · 25 SLA-breached" on a day Meta delivered leads — two counters, two stories, neither reconciled. And the thing that has not moved a millimeter in five days: compliance is still 0/7. b3 (Texas telephone-solicitor registration) and b7 (your CA producer-license # on the six live creatives) are the exact two the last ad account was banned for, and TX and CA are exactly the states in the pile you're dialing. Today has two moves, one each. Frankie: the two numbers, or a written rule that scopes the dialing to states that don't need them. Chitraksh: put one real lead all the way through to a booking so cost-per-booked-call becomes a number instead of a dash.
source: Reconstructed from a live Gmail sweep of hanfluxai@gmail.com through 2026-09-02T09:00Z, plus the on-disk workspace. Meeting-ingest failed again Sep 2 00:02Z ("no desktop bridge in this session at all") — meeting_brief_lines.json now 13d stale (Aug 20). Dashboard still v15.17 (Aug 28). spotlight.title: Day five of dialing TX + CA leads with b3 and b7 still open — close it or scope it, today
spotlight.detail: Nothing about this has improved since the Sep 1 brief; it has only aged. Compliance is 0/7, the two items that bite are b3 (TX telephone-solicitor registration) and b7 (your CA producer-license # on the six live creatives and the landing page), and those are the precise two the predecessor ad account was banned for. The pile you are working is CA/TX/NV/ID/NJ — Texas and California are in it. There are exactly two acceptable end-states by tonight and both are cheap: (a) send Chitraksh your NPN + CA producer-license # so the creatives and page get papered today, or (b) write one line — "we call NV/ID only until b3+b7 are placed" — and follow it. What is not acceptable is a sixth day of neither. This is the single move that repeats the ban.

spotlight.title: $168 spent, 15 leads, zero confirmed booked calls — the deciding metric is a dash, not a number
spotlight.detail: The watchdog is not hiding this; it states it in every scorecard: "Booked calls (CRM) — no CRM source connected," "Cost / booked call — not evaluable," and "cost per booked call is the deciding metric — CPL flatters volume and does not decide." The separate Meta→CRM hourly sync has been failing since Aug 27 23:47Z and has not been re-checked. So the $11.18 CPL that looks healthy is measuring the wrong thing, and 56% of the plan is gone while the only question that matters — does a lead become a call — has never once been answered. Today's build: connect the CRM source (or stand up the simplest possible substitute) and push ONE real lead end-to-end into the F·A Apex booking flow. One completed path turns the dash into a number before the second half of the budget burns.

spotlight.title: Fifteen leads, two counters that disagree, and a "call fast" form that now ships leads with no phone
spotlight.detail: Ben Garcia (TX) arrived 8:19 PM PT last night with an email address and the field "Call — no number" — the second recent lead unreachable by the playbook the whole campaign is built on. On the same day, the AURA digest reported "0 new leads in 24h" alongside 25 SLA-breached and a 13% booking rate, while Meta was delivering — two systems telling two different stories about the same company. Three fixes, none big: make phone a required field on the instant form; reconcile the notifier count against the watchdog's 15 and against Meta; and do one written triage pass over all 15 — which state, which consent, call now or hold — including the lead already flagged "no TCPA consent, call by hand, no AI/text."
